title: [MIG-004] Make configuration, runtime assets and service composition project-independent
objective: Run the same installed library against different projects without reading the library source checkout, leaking state or restoring hidden defaults.
inScope: Implement MIG-002's validated project configuration and a common composition factory/service graph. Pass the same task registry, lifecycle/assignment/evidence/run stores, context sources, validator resolver and provider/policy adapters into start, validation, all reviews/rework, PR/readiness/merge, CLI, status, diagnostics and recovery.

Fix registry/evidence/manual-adapter schema resolution to use package-owned immutable assets. Keep supported project schema extension/override semantics explicit; do not silently trust arbitrary project files as core schemas. Project requirements/contracts/tasks still resolve at their required exact source revision.

Replace npm-only assumptions with configured validator commands/executors and literal arguments, scoped working directories and explicit toolchain preflight. Preserve a documented npm profile without imposing it on non-Node consumers.

Validate canonical roots and project/worktree identity, containment/symlink behavior, worktree locks, shared-state rules and unsupported filesystem durability. No hidden process.cwd fallback when an explicit project is selected; never write into node_modules or change the current project accidentally.

Provide non-destructive config/init/doctor primitives for #78's guided setup: preview intended files, refuse overwrites, validate missing inputs and keep credentials host-injected. Installation itself must perform no project mutation.

**Expected surfaces:** Configuration schema/loader, shared composition factory, all createLocal* factories, schema asset resolver, validator and context sources, CLI adapter wiring, diagnostics/recovery.
outOfScope: No new lifecycle/review authority, automatic agent launcher, source consumer cutover or second independent setup/driver implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-01: One configured project context reaches every gate/store/adapter; a sentinel configuration test detects any nested factory reverting to repository defaults.
AC-02: The runtime works without copied core schemas in the consumer and from an unrelated current working directory.
AC-03: Two projects with identical task IDs and distinct roots cannot share locks, state, evidence or exchange by accident; invalid/escaping roots reject before writes.
AC-04: A non-npm consumer executes only its declared validators; Windows paths with spaces and command arguments work without shell interpolation.
AC-05: Current role context, exact-revision artifacts, history durability and fail-closed behavior are preserved.
AC-06: Initialization is repeatable/non-destructive and doctor reports missing tools, assets, config or incompatible storage clearly.
validationPlan:
Installed-style fixture tests for renamed paths, alternate cwd, missing assets/config, read-only installation, symlink/path escape and overlapping IDs. Exercise nonempty requirements/contracts through UAT and all configured state readers/writers. Verify rejected operations cause no provider calls or state mutations.

Use applicable repository build/test/schema/contract checks. Retain exact commands/results, package/source/config identities and an acceptance-to-evidence map. Existing or fake-provider fixtures are not independent live review or task-completion evidence. This task is normal feature work, not a new canary requirement.
npm run build; npm test; python schemas/validate_fixtures.py; python schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py; npm run test:adversarial:mutations. Add issue-specific checks before admission.
